highlight.title: GCSE Results App Goes National for Summer 2026
highlight.summary: All Year 11 students in England can now access their GCSE results via the new Education Record app from summer 2026, following successful regional pilots. The app is estimated to save schools £30 million per year in administrative costs.

resources.title: BBC Bitesize Exam Revision App
resources.why_now: Students can access comprehensive flashcards, quizzes and revision guides for GCSE and A-Level subjects ahead of May exam season, with over 1.5 million students using it weekly.

resources.title: Oak National Academy KS3-4 Teaching Resources
resources.why_now: Parents and teachers can access free structured lesson plans and resources for Years 7-11, including the new science curriculum that improves student engagement through better sequencing.

resources.title: Mobile Phones in Schools - Updated DfE Guidance
resources.why_now: Parents need to understand the January 2026 guidance update requiring schools to be 'phone-free by default' and how this impacts their children's school day.

resources.title: GCSE Results Day 2026 Information
resources.why_now: Students and parents should prepare for GCSE results day on Thursday 20 August 2026, including new digital access options and what to do if results aren't as expected.

claude_take: The big story this week is the GCSE results app finally going national after patchy pilot uptake, which could genuinely help families manage academic records long-term. However, the stricter mobile phone guidance feels more significant for day-to-day school life, as Ofsted will now check these policies during inspections.
